name: microbial_island
description: MacArthur-Wilson equilibrium model in a microbial regime: a large mainland taxa pool, fast colonization + extinction (high turnover), and a shallow area-extinction exponent giving the observed flat microbial taxa-area slope (z ~ 0.02-0.1; Horner-Devine 2004, Bell 2005). Reuses MacArthurWilsonEquilibriumProcess with no new process.

n_pool.description: Mainland taxa-pool size P (large for microbes)

colonization_base.description: Per-taxon colonization prob at distance 0 (fast dispersal)

extinction_base.description: Per-taxon extinction prob at the reference area (fast local turnover)

area_max.description: Largest patch area (= reference area for extinction)

distance_min.description: Least isolated patch distance (linear across islands)

distance_max.description: Most isolated patch distance (0 = isolation held fixed)

area_exponent.description: Area-extinction exponent; low -> flat microbial taxa-area slope z

seed.description: RNG seed; each island uses seed + its index

island_00.doc:
One island under the canonical MacArthur-Wilson equilibrium model.

The phenomenological colonization/extinction model of *The Theory of Island
Biogeography* (MacArthur & Wilson 1963, 1967), as a counterpart to the
mechanistic Lotka-Volterra :class:`IslandProcess`. A mainland pool of
``n_pool`` species feeds the island; each species is present (1) or absent
(0). Each generation every absent species colonizes with probability
``c = colonization_base / (1 + distance)`` and every present species goes
extinct with probability ``e = extinction_base * (ref_area/area)**area_exponent``.

Richness relaxes to S* = P*c/(c+e): larger area (lower ``e``) and lower
isolation (higher ``c``) both raise it, and species identity turns over even
once S has plateaued (the turnover prediction). Immigration I(S)=(P-S)c
falls with S and extinction E(S)=S*e rises with S; they cross at S* — the
rate-crossing diagram.

Outputs (all deltas, so the stores accumulate to absolute values — the
mass/length delta precedent used throughout this workspace):

presence : map[string, float]
    Per-species occupancy delta (+1 colonization, -1 extinction); the store
    accumulates to a 0/1 occupancy vector.
richness : float
    Local richness delta; accumulates to the absolute present-species count.
cum_colonizations, cum_extinctions : float
    Per-tick gross colonization / extinction counts, emitted as deltas so
    the stores accumulate to running totals (their first difference per tick
    is the gross turnover, from which the per-S event rates are measured).

_contract.description: type(name, bases, dict, **kwds) -> a new type

emitter.doc:
Store historical states in memory.

``subsample`` records only every Nth composite tick (default 1 =
every tick). Use this for long runs or composites with heavy
state (large fields, many agents) to keep RAM bounded — the
saved time-series still reflects the simulation's true cadence
via each row's ``global_time`` field.

``max_len`` optionally bounds ``history`` to the most recent N
recorded rows (a ring buffer): once the cap is reached each new
record drops the oldest. Default ``None`` = unbounded (the
historical behaviour — consumers such as v2ecoli that read the
full ``history`` are unaffected unless they opt in). ``max_len``
counts *recorded* rows (i.e. post-``subsample``).

_contract.description: type(name, bases, dict, **kwds) -> a new type
